_purpose: Citywide OPERATING budget context for the Data & Methods popover — how big the transportation spending categories are against the whole City operating budget. Manual, reviewed input (mill-rates pattern): NOT auto-fetched, NOT part of the weekly refresh. Reaches the frontend through status.json via generate_status.budget_context(), and the pod simply never shows if this file is unreadable.
_scope: ⚠️ THIS IS A CITYWIDE HEADLINE STAT AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED TO THE SPATIAL PIPELINE. It answers 'how much does the City spend on this in total', not 'what does this neighbourhood cost'. Its road figures are derived over the ~11,000 km CITYWIDE network, which INCLUDES arterials — the neighbourhood lens excludes arterials by decision, so the two use different denominators and MUST NOT share a constant. Nothing here is imported by src/ or main.py.
_basis: ⚠️ EVERY LINE IS OPERATING ONLY — maintenance, snow clearing and service delivery. Capital is excluded throughout: road reconstruction, asphalt overlay and the Neighbourhood Renewal Program on the roads side; new trains, garages and line extensions on the transit side. The categories are therefore comparable TO EACH OTHER but none of them is a total cost. Never let this table be read as 'what transportation costs Edmonton'.

source.document: City of Edmonton Budget FAQ / Open Budget — 2025 expenditure breakdown
source.retrieved: 2026-08-03 (relayed, not fetched from the Oracle box)
source.note: Quoted publicly as '$3.8 billion'; the precise figure is $3,845,555 thousand.
source.corroborated: ✅ CHECKED 2026-08-04 against the Open Budget portal (DATA.md §17), because every share in this table divides by it and it had been relayed: the portal's FY2025 TAX-SUPPORTED expenses total $3,855,881,010 — this value is 99.73% of that, a $10.3M gap. Independently confirmed, not merely restated.

total_operating_budget.scope_is_tax_supported: ⚠️ THIS IS THE TAX-SUPPORTED OPERATING BUDGET, NOT ALL FUNDS, and that is the CORRECT denominator here rather than a limitation. The portal's FY2025 all-funds total is $4,203,648,909 — the difference is Utilities ($235,789,773) and Enterprise/CRL ($111,978,126). All four numerators in this table (transit, roads, bike lanes, sidewalks) are tax-supported, so dividing them by an all-funds total would understate every share (transit would read 11.15% instead of 12.18%, roads 2.44% instead of 2.67%). ⚠️ The pod's lead line says "the City's $3.8B 2025 operating budget" — if that copy is ever reworded, do NOT let it imply all funds.

categories.label: Transit (incl. DATS)
categories.source: ETS 2024/2025 Annual Service Plan, Appendix A Financial Summary (2025 budget, $000s)
categories.note: Gross operating expense before the ~$156.3M of fare and other revenue. ⚠️ Includes DATS here, unlike the per-acre transit cost column, which excludes it because DATS runs no scheduled stops — see city_unit_costs.json transit_ets.chosen_numerator. The two numbers are for different questions and are SUPPOSED to differ.

categories.label: Roads
categories.source: Maintenance: City of Edmonton Open Budget portal (budget.edmonton.ca/api/operating_budget.csv), branch 'Parks & Roads Services', program 'Roadway Maintenance', FY2017 — $65,671,000, tax-supported expenses. Snow: Taproot Edmonton reporting quoting City infrastructure field operations staff.
categories.maintenance_replaced_a_derived_figure: ⚠️ THIS COMPONENT WAS $14,135,000 UNTIL 2026-08-04 AND THAT FIGURE WAS ABOUT 5x TOO LOW. It was derived as $1,285/km x ~11,000 km — a narrow unit rate multiplied across the whole network and labelled 'roads maintenance'. The published program implies roughly $5,900/km. The error was in OUR derivation, not in the Taproot source: that source's TOTALS reconcile (see snow_cross_check), only the rate-times-network product did not. Replaced with the published program line above.
categories.why_the_2017_vintage: ⚠️ 2017 IS THE ONLY YEAR EDMONTON EVER PUBLISHED A ROADS-ONLY MAINTENANCE PROGRAM, so a stale vintage is the price of a clean scope. The program tree was re-cut in 2018 (roads maintenance folded into 'OPS/PARS - Infrastructure Maintenance', which also covers sidewalks, pathways and bridges) and re-cut again in 2026 (folded into 'OPS/PARS - Mobility Infrastructure Services'). Using the 2018-2025 line would DOUBLE-COUNT against this table's own sidewalks and bike-lane rows. Peter's call 2026-08-04: roads-only scope beats matching vintage, documented rather than silently mixed — the same call already made for ETS 2025 vs fire 2026 in city_unit_costs.json. ⚠️ Being 2017 dollars, this is if anything a LOWER bound on today's spend: the branch grew ~34% (244.9 -> 327.1 $M) between 2017 and 2025.
categories.snow_cross_check: ✅ The snow figures are INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED by the same Open Budget portal: this row's $36.85M roads snow plus the active-transport row's $30.15M path snow = $67.0M, against the published 'Snow and Ice Control' program at $67,553,815 (FY2025) — 99.2%. That agreement is why the snow components were left untouched, and the contrast with the maintenance component is what exposed it.
categories.portal_vs_pdf: ⚠️ The Open Budget portal and the Approved Operating Budget PDF do not tie exactly: the portal's FY2026 branch total for Parks and Roads Services is $307,325,053 against the PDF's $303,361,000 gross, +1.31%. Small, but do not present portal and PDF figures as the same series. The PDF is branch-level only and bundles parks with roads, which is why it cannot source this row at all.

categories.label: Bike lanes & pathways
categories.note: Snow clearing is 99% of it — a 24-hour bare-pavement service standard over ~1,500 km. That network also covers pedestrian squares, bus stops, LRT platforms and staircases, so it is broader than bikeways alone.

categories.label: Sidewalks
categories.source: Taproot Edmonton, quoting the City: 'the city is responsible for almost 5,776 linear kilometres of sidewalks and spends $5.9 million on their maintenance each year'
categories.note: Confirmed a SEPARATE, non-overlapping category from the active-transport line above — sidewalks are not in the 1,500 km snow-clearing network, which the source enumerates explicitly. The two lines are safely additive.

excluded_from_the_table.label: Active Transportation Acceleration project
excluded_from_the_table.reason: ⚠️ NOT ADDITIVE with the bike-lane line above and therefore left out of the comparison rather than shown beside it. It is capital debt service plus incremental maintenance for NEW build-out; the $30.42M line is the cost of running what already exists. Adding them answers no question. Kept here so the figure is not lost (City's own stated number, Budget FAQ).

_ratios_are_derived_not_pinned: ⚠️ DO NOT hardcode the comparison ratios. They are computed from the values above so they cannot drift out of agreement with them. This matters: the research brief this table came from claimed 'transit is roughly 15x the road ops budget and roughly 90x the entire active-transportation network' — both wrong, because the ratios had slid one row. Actual: transit is 4.6x roads, 15.4x active transport and 79.4x sidewalks. Bike lanes plus sidewalks together are 0.94% of the operating budget, which is the one claim that held. ⚠️ THE ROADS RATIO ITSELF HAS NOW MOVED ONCE — it read 9.2x from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-04, on a roads-maintenance component that was ~5x too low (see the roads category). That is the second time a number in this table changed after publication, and the reason nothing here is pinned: because the UI divides, both corrections propagated by editing one dollar value.
